answers.question: Black Friday 2025: how deep did Sony cut its 65" TVs on Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy against rivals, and did it buy Amazon rank?
answers.chip: Black Friday 2025 · Amazon + Walmart + Best Buy
steps: Loading 20 Amazon listings' daily history (price, stock, Best Sellers Rank, bought-in-past-month)
Loading Walmart and Best Buy daily readings from the retailer feed
Setting the baseline (Oct 1, 2025 – Nov 13, 2025) and Black Friday week (Nov 21, 2025 – Dec 1, 2025)
Comparing 25 model–retailer pairs on lowest price, autumn change and discount off MSRP
Reading the Amazon sales-rank response to each price move
Ranking the movers and drafting the recommended moves
answers.headline: Sony cut -18.0% on Amazon, -10.8% on Walmart, -7.3% on Best Buy for Black Friday 2025, landing 26% off MSRP on average, #3 of 5 brands for depth; TCL went deepest at 37% off. On Amazon, BRAVIA 5 went $1298.00 → $998.00 and ranked #9,712 → #3,340.
answers.what: TCL 37% off MSRP · Hisense 30% off MSRP · Sony 26% off MSRP · LG 21% off MSRP · Samsung 18% off MSRP. 7 of 9 Sony model–retailer pairs were cut 5% or more.
answers.why: Black Friday is a price-match week for TVs: the same model lands within a few dollars across retailers. Sony's widest gap was BRAVIA 5: $998.00 at Amazon vs $999.99 at Best Buy. Rivals averaged 29% off MSRP against Sony's 26%, so Sony stayed the premium shelf.
answers.when: Black Friday was Nov 28, 2025. Black Friday week: Nov 21, 2025 – Dec 1, 2025. Baseline: Oct 1, 2025 – Nov 13, 2025. 2026 models launched after Black Friday 2025 are not in this comparison.
answers.insight: Sony's Black Friday cuts bought rank: BRAVIA 5 climbed #9,712 → #3,340 on Amazon at 33% off MSRP. The question for 2026 is depth, not whether to play.

answers.question: Is the same Sony TV priced the same at Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy and Target, and how deep does Sony discount off MSRP against rivals?
answers.chip: Channel pricing · same TV, every retailer
steps: Taking each model's median price over Jul 27, 2026 – Oct 25, 2026 at every retailer that sells it
Matching 20 models across Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy and Target by model number
Setting aside 3 retailer prices more than 35% from the model's median (a different variant or a list price, not a street price)
Measuring the gap between each model's cheapest and dearest retailer
Restating every price as a discount off MSRP
Ranking 5 brands on discount depth
answers.headline: Sony sells 5% below MSRP at the median, #5 of 5 brands for discount depth (Hisense deepest at 29%). Its widest channel gap is BRAVIA 8 II: Amazon $2498.00 vs Target $3299.00 (32.1%).
answers.what: Hisense 29% off · TCL 28% off · LG 22% off · Samsung 9% off · Sony 5% off. Sony is cheapest at Amazon on 2 of 4 models sold at more than one retailer.
answers.why: Sony's channel gaps average 9.0% against 12.6% for rivals. A gap that wide is visible to any shopper with two tabs open, and on TVs it is usually a retailer holding last month's price after a rival cut.
answers.when: Jul 27, 2026 – Oct 25, 2026 (13 weeks). Medians use only days a retailer price was read. Set aside: Samsung S90H at Target ($2499.00); TCL QM7K at Amazon ($1319.00); Hisense U8 at Best Buy ($1869.00).
answers.insight: Sony holds a tighter price across retailers than its rivals, so its pricing lever is depth: it sits 5% off MSRP against Hisense's 29%.

answers.question: Prime Big Deal Days: who discounted, on which retailer, and did the cuts actually buy Amazon sales rank?
answers.chip: Prime Big Deal Days · cut vs hold
steps: Pulling daily Amazon prices and Best Sellers Rank for 19 Amazon listings
Pulling Walmart prices for 19 listings from the Walmart feed
Comparing Oct 13, 2026 – Oct 14, 2026 with the 14 days before
Measuring each listing's sales-rank response to its own price move
Separating the brands that cut and climbed from the ones that held
answers.headline: Sony largely held price on Prime Big Deal Days (+5.4% on average, 1 of 8 listings cut 3%+) while Hisense moved -3.5%. The clearest payoff from cutting was Hisense's U7: cut 23.4% and #2,263 → #1,086 on Amazon.
answers.what: Sony +5.4% (1/8 cut) · Samsung +0.9% (0/8 cut) · LG -0.4% (0/7 cut) · TCL +2.3% (0/7 cut) · Hisense -3.5% (2/8 cut).
answers.why: Prime Big Deal Days is an Amazon event, so the cuts land on Amazon: across the set Amazon listings moved +0.3% and Walmart +1.6%. Sony's lead Amazon listing (BRAVIA 3 II) moved +5.9% and ranked #3,131 → #2,852.
answers.when: Prime Big Deal Days: Oct 13, 2026 – Oct 14, 2026. Baseline: Sep 29, 2026 – Oct 12, 2026. Rank read through Oct 16, 2026.
answers.insight: Holding price on Prime Big Deal Days cost Sony nothing in rank: its lead listing held #2,852 without a deal, so the margin it kept was free.

answers.question: What drives Sony's praise and complaints, and is reliability a Sony problem or the category's?
steps: Counting 1,154 aspect mentions across Amazon and Walmart reviews
Scoring 6 aspects for 5 brands
Reading 135 Sony Walmart reviews for the sharpest complaints
Measuring Amazon review velocity from daily review counts, one count per shared review pool
Benchmarking each weak aspect against the best competitor
answers.headline: Shoppers love Sony's picture quality (89% positive) and complain about reliability (36% positive, against LG's 47%). It rates 4.43★, #3 of 5.
answers.what: Picture quality 89% · Setup 88% · Quality 80% · Sound quality 80% · Value for money 78% · Reliability 36%.
answers.why: Reliability is where the brand loses: 62 negative mentions against 35 positive. LG scores 47% on the same aspect, so the complaint is about the product, not the category.
answers.when: Amazon review summaries as read on the build date; Walmart reviews from Apr 5, 2025 to Oct 15, 2026.
answers.insight: Sony's rating rests on picture quality and setup, and it adds new Amazon reviews faster than 0 of the set (341 this quarter). Reliability is the one attribute where a competitor proves the category can do better (LG 47%), so it is a product fix, not a messaging one.

answers.headline: Sony holds 15.2% of brand mentions in AI answers, #5 of 5; Samsung leads at 18.6%. It is named in 48 of 72 answers, most often by Claude (23 of 24).
answers.what: Samsung 18.6% · TCL 18.3% · LG 17.9% · Hisense 17.5% · Sony 15.2%. Since Oct 27, 2026 Sony moved 0 points.
answers.why: Being named is not being recommended: of the 51 answers that commit to one top pick, LG gets 19, Sony 7. ChatGPT names Sony least often (12 of 24), so that is where the gap is widest.
answers.insight: Sony is known to the engines but rarely chosen: named in 48 of 72 answers yet the top pick in 7 of the 51 that commit to one brand. Closing the gap is about being the recommended answer, which comes from comparison and review content the engines cite, not from more mentions.
